items.title: Russian Defence Ministry says overnight strikes hit military-linked facilities across Ukraine
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its overnight missile-and-drone attack struck defence-industry enterprises, storage terminals, energy sites and transport infrastructure in Kyiv and five Ukrainian regions, including Lviv and Ivano-Frankivsk. The ministry described the targets as connected to Ukraine's armed forces; its statement did not establish the extent of damage.

items.title: Reports describe emergency power cuts in Lviv and outages in Kryvyi Rih
items.summary: Emergency electricity outages were reported in Lviv and power losses in Kryvyi Rih following the overnight strikes. Trolleybus services were also reportedly suspended in several Kyiv districts, adding to disruption after the attacks.

items.title: Russia says air defences intercepted 310 Ukrainian drones overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry reported that its air defences shot down 310 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions during the night. The statement did not provide a regional breakdown or independently assessed damage figures.

items.title: Luhansk authorities report three killed in Ukrainian drone attack on residential buildings
items.summary: Russian-installed Luhansk leader Leonid Pasechnik said a Ukrainian drone attack struck apartment buildings in Yuvileine near Luhansk, killing three people and injuring six, including a child. Concrete floors reportedly collapsed in one building, and rescuers were searching for people who might remain trapped.

items.title: Russian deputy foreign minister rejects even quasi-NATO membership for Ukraine
items.summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said that even a form of quasi-membership for Ukraine in NATO would be unacceptable to Moscow. His statement underscores Russia's opposition to security arrangements resembling alliance membership.

items.title: Russia says no agreement reached on next round of Ukraine negotiations
items.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said there is no agreement on holding another round of negotiations over Ukraine. He gave the statement in response to a question about the next stage of talks.

items.title: NABU and SAPO announce bribery suspicions involving former SBU official
items.summary: NABU and SAPO say a former Ukrainian Security Service unit chief is suspected of leaking confidential investigative information in exchange for benefits, including a BMW X5 and a family hotel stay valued at 160,000 hryvnias. A business associate linked to the Privat group and a former Ukrgasvydobuvannya executive also received notices of suspicion; the investigation remains ongoing.

items.title: Poland investigates possible airspace violations during Russian attack on Ukraine
items.summary: Polish military authorities are reportedly investigating two possible airspace violations during the overnight Russian strikes on Ukraine. An unidentified flying object was found near Lipowiec in eastern Poland after radar indications of a possible fall in Bilgoraj County; Rzeszow airport temporarily suspended operations.

items.title: Report alleges three Kyiv water utility workers killed during missile strikes
items.summary: A Russian military-linked account says three Kyivvodokanal employees were killed and about 15 people injured when critical infrastructure was hit during the overnight strikes on Kyiv. The same account reports fires at an office building and other sites; the casualty figures are attributed to that report.

items.title: Russia identifies alleged missile-production and transport targets in overnight attack
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its overnight strikes hit a Fire Point missile assembly facility near Kyiv, an aircraft plant in Lviv allegedly producing Flamingo missiles, and the Zatoka road-rail bridge in Odesa region. These specific target claims expand on its earlier general account of the attack; the ministry did not provide an independently established damage assessment.

items.title: Ukraine says nuclear plants reduced output after strikes on power grid
items.summary: Ukraine's Energy Ministry said nuclear power plants were forced to reduce electricity generation after overnight strikes damaged power stations, substations and transmission infrastructure. The plants themselves were not reported to have been directly hit.

items.title: DTEK reports over 41,000 customers without power in Odesa region
items.summary: Ukrainian energy company DTEK reported that an attack on one of its facilities in Odesa region left more than 41,000 customers without electricity. The outage adds to disruption from the wider overnight strikes.

items.title: Medvedev rejects proposal to trade Ukrainian territory for NATO membership
items.summary: Former Russian president Dmitry Medvedev dismissed the idea of Ukraine joining a revised NATO in exchange for territorial concessions as absurd. He reiterated Moscow's opposition to Ukraine entering the alliance and suggested that such a trade would be unacceptable.

items.title: Russia says it will raise Luhansk residential drone strike with UN and OSCE
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry plans to immediately submit materials concerning the reported Ukrainian drone strike on residential buildings in Yuvileine, Luhansk, to Russian representatives at the United Nations and OSCE, according to official Rodion Miroshnik. Local authorities earlier reported three deaths and six injuries.

items.title: SAPO reports bail set in alleged Transnistria draft-evasion smuggling case
items.summary: SAPO says Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court set bail at 500,000 hryvnias for a suspect investigators consider the organizer of a scheme to smuggle military-age men through Transnistria into Europe. The court also imposed travel and reporting restrictions; investigators have completed the pretrial investigation and opened case materials to the defence.

items.title: Ryabkov says European visit to Moscow would not join Ukraine talks format
items.summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Moscow could promptly arrange a visit by representatives of three European countries if they accept its invitation. He stressed that the invitation does not mean European representatives would join the existing Russia-US-Ukraine negotiating format.

items.title: Smolensk governor reports damage to energy site and home after Ukrainian attack
items.summary: Smolensk regional governor Vasily Anokhin said an overnight large-scale Ukrainian attack damaged an energy facility, a civilian industrial site and a private residence in the Russian region. His statement did not specify casualties or the extent of the damage.

items.title: Kyiv water supply disrupted after strikes damage utility infrastructure
items.summary: Local utility services reportedly said Kyivvodokanal facilities were damaged and attacks on the power system disrupted water supplies in the capital. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged residents to work remotely where possible because of damaged bridges, while emergency power cuts were also reported in Dnipropetrovsk region.

items.title: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell on its territory
items.summary: Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone fell in Poland during the overnight attack on Ukraine. He identified debris from a Kh-101 missile near Nowy Lipowiec, another missile near Rudnik nad Sanem and a drone near Molodycz; no casualties or damage were reported.

items.title: Russia claims 6,808 Ukrainian drones intercepted over the past week
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted 6,808 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones, 13 Flamingo missiles and eight Neptune missiles over the past week. It also claimed two large-scale and 11 group strikes against Ukrainian military-industrial, energy and airfield targets, without providing independently established damage figures.

items.title: Water supply halted in Vyshneve amid Kyiv sewer restrictions
items.summary: The local water utility reportedly halted water supply in Vyshneve, Kyiv region, after Kyiv's sewer network restricted wastewater intake following the overnight attack. The disruption adds to water and power service problems reported around the capital.

items.title: Estonia reportedly plans to close all road border crossings with Russia on December 1
items.summary: Estonia's government reportedly decided to close all road border checkpoints with Russia from December 1. Latvia's border guard chief warned the move could redirect traffic toward Latvian crossings and increase staffing demands.

items.title: Moldovan parliament advances military-technical cooperation agreement with Ukraine
items.summary: Moldova's parliament reportedly approved a first reading of an agreement with Ukraine covering military equipment maintenance, cyber defence, critical infrastructure protection, training and non-lethal equipment. The proposal is not yet final legislation.

items.title: Tusk says US allies want to avoid escalation after missiles and drone fell in Poland
items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incidents in Polish airspace require a response but that allies including the United States are reluctant to risk a further escalation. He said he does not always agree with Washington's assessment of such incidents.

items.title: Putin calls on Ukrainians to seek closer ties with Russia
items.summary: In remarks aired on Russian television, President Vladimir Putin urged Ukrainians to consider their children's future and move toward closer ties with Russia. He accused Ukraine's nationalist leadership and Western supporters of acting against Ukrainians' interests.

items.title: Russian military commentary says Kyiv bridges remain usable after strikes
items.summary: A Russian military-linked assessment said traffic had largely resumed across Kyiv's bridges after the overnight attack, although some crossings still faced restrictions. The account acknowledged that the strikes had not caused bridge collapses or critical structural damage.

items.title: Britain and Norway reportedly plan two missile-armed patrol boats for Ukraine
items.summary: Britain and Norway reportedly plan to share more than £100 million in costs to build two 30-metre fast combat boats for Ukraine's navy at British shipyards. The vessels are expected to carry missiles and air-defence systems under the countries' maritime support initiative, although construction and delivery dates were not specified.

items.title: Russia claims daytime strikes on Ukrainian logistics, energy and port facilities
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said drone strikes hit a military-linked logistics centre in Horodnia, Chernihiv region, the Slobozhanska thermal power facility in Kharkiv region, and a cargo ship and port infrastructure in Chornomorsk, Odesa region. It also claimed a locomotive used for military supplies was struck near Riadove in Dnipropetrovsk region.

items.title: Report describes Russia's new Kub-10ME long-range attack drone
items.summary: Russian forces have reportedly begun using the Kub-10ME loitering munition, described as having a range exceeding 100 kilometres and optoelectronic guidance for moving targets. Its manufacturer claims day-and-night operation and improved resistance to electronic warfare; the reported specifications do not establish its battlefield effectiveness.

items.title: Russia summons Romanian ambassador over visas denied to young taekwondo athletes
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry said it summoned Romania's ambassador on November 20 to protest the refusal of entry visas to its youth taekwondo team for European championships in Bucharest. Moscow called the decision nationality-based discrimination and warned of consequences, amid wider restrictions affecting Russian participation in international sport.
